one_liner: A wide-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 1.9x fair value. Interesting below about $34.

profile.what: Charles Schwab is the largest US brokerage by client assets, serving individual investors and the independent financial advisers who custody client money with it. It absorbed TD Ameritrade in 2020.
profile.money: Net interest income from investing client cash balances is about half of revenue; the rest is asset-management fees, trading revenue and bank deposit fees. It makes more money when interest rates are higher and when clients keep more cash with it.
profile.valued: Schwab is valued on P/E. The multiple moves with interest rates and with client cash balances, which shrank when rates rose and clients moved money into higher-yielding funds.
profile.peer_group: Financials · bank, insurer or asset manager

summary.sentence: The largest retail brokerage, with earnings sensitive to interest rates and client cash.
strengths: Earnings have more than doubled from their 2023 low.

meaning.what_it_does: The largest US retail brokerage and custodian for independent advisers.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Interest on client cash, asset-management fees and trading revenue.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Scale lets it offer the lowest prices, which attracts more assets.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: Clients move cash out of low-yielding accounts, as they did in 2022-23.

valuation.method: Banks are valued on book value, not free cash flow. Justified price-to-book = (ROE − 3% growth) ÷ (required return − 3%), using a normalised ROE of 14.2% (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM, capped at 25%) and a required return of 11% (low) to 9% (high): 1.40–1.87 × book value per share of $29.71.

methods.name: Excess-return model on book value
methods.basis: Book value per share $29.71 × 1.40–1.87. This is how Damodaran values banks and insurers: equity is worth book value plus the returns earned above the cost of equity.
